statement: Legion Capital processed 10.0 million payment transactions worth about ₹1,500 crore in September 2026 (average ₹1,500).
Arvanta Payments charges a blended fee of 0.20% of payment volume.
Brevis Pay's final quote (15 Sep 2026) is a blended fee of 0.176% of volume, 12% below Arvanta.
Brevis Pay's India-only hosting add-on, needed to keep fraud scoring in India, costs a flat ₹6 lakh a month.
The one-time cost of migrating to Brevis Pay (engineering, certification, testing) is estimated at ₹40 lakh.
Treasury estimates that Brevis Pay's T+1 card settlement (vs Arvanta's T+2) would cut funding cost by about ₹4 lakh a month on the 40% slice.
Legion Capital's cost of funds is 9.5% a year.
Dispute handling fees: Arvanta ₹150 and Brevis ₹250 per dispute. About 2,000 disputes a month arise on the 40% slice.
FY27 payments-cost budget is ₹33 crore; the current run-rate is ₹36 crore a year (9% over budget).
Payment volume is forecast to grow 25% over the next 12 months.
The board's FY27 target is to cut the cost-to-income ratio from 48% to 42%.
An early internal email (March 2026) estimated that Brevis would be 18% cheaper than Arvanta.
30 cross-border SME merchants in the sales pipeline, worth about ₹45 crore a month, need international card acceptance, which only Brevis Pay supports.
FY27 OKR: no single payment gateway should carry more than 70% of volume by 31 March 2027.
Competitor Vireo Finance moved to a multi-gateway setup in June 2026 and now advertises '99.9% payment uptime' to SME merchants.
Legion Pay Later (BNPL at checkout) is planned for Q1 FY28 (Apr–Jun 2027). Brevis Pay has native EMI/BNPL APIs; Arvanta would need a 4-month custom build.
Arvanta has offered an 8% fee cut if Legion commits 100% of volume for 3 more years.
Expected fee revenue from the cross-border pipeline is about ₹1.08 crore a year (0.2% take rate on ₹45 crore a month).
Two of Legion's top five co-lending partners already settle through Brevis Pay.
In Q2–Q3 FY27, 70% of lost SME deals cited lack of international card acceptance.
The board wants cross-border card acceptance live by 31 March 2027.
Arvanta's 14 June 2026 outage delayed ₹2.3 crore of loan collections; ₹11 lakh of wrongly charged late fees had to be waived for 1,900 borrowers.
Brevis Pay is 3 years old with about 1,200 merchants; Arvanta is 9 years old with about 40,000 merchants.
Settlement-delay complaints about Arvanta rose from 120 (July) to 210 (August) to 340 (September 2026).
Four large merchants (M-104, M-221, M-307, M-412), together about ₹38 crore a month, have threatened to leave over settlement delays.
About 900 failed EMI auto-debit complaints arrive each month; in 14% of them the borrower was wrongly charged a late fee.
In the Brevis pilot (2% of traffic, Aug–Sep 2026), mobile checkout conversion was 3.1 points higher than on Arvanta.
During the pilot, complaints from Coral Bank and Tamra Bank customers were 40% higher on Brevis than on Arvanta.
Legion's merchant NPS is 41 against an industry benchmark of 50.
Average refund turnaround is 5.2 days on Arvanta and 3.0 days on Brevis (pilot).
Brevis checkout supports 11 Indian languages; Arvanta supports 4.
Monthly merchant churn was 2.1% in September 2026, up from 1.4% in Q1 FY27.
20 of 340 settlement complaints in September (about 6%) breached the 30-day grievance-resolution limit.
22% of 1-star app reviews in Q3 mention 'payment failed'.
Each support ticket costs about ₹180 to handle.
Arvanta MSA: a ₹25 lakh early-exit fee applies if Legion's volume with Arvanta falls below 80% (the minimum commitment) before 31 March 2028.
Arvanta MSA: Legion must give 90 days' written notice before reducing volume.
Arvanta MSA renews automatically for 2 years unless notice is given 6 months before 31 March 2028.
The Brevis draft agreement has no clause on where data is stored or processed.
Brevis draft caps liability at 3 months' fees; Arvanta's cap is 12 months' fees.
Brevis draft lets Brevis change prices with 30 days' notice.
Brevis draft uses Singapore law with arbitration in Singapore; Arvanta's contract uses Indian law and Mumbai courts.
The Brevis draft gives no audit or inspection rights to Legion or the RBI. Legion's policy and RBI outsourcing norms require them.
Arvanta's data processing agreement (aligned to the DPDP Act 2023) is signed; Brevis has not yet provided one.
Brevis indemnifies only for 'gross negligence'; Arvanta indemnifies for 'negligence'.
Both Arvanta (since 2021) and Brevis (since 2025) are RBI-authorised payment aggregators.

statement: Brevis Pay's fraud-scoring sub-processor, Sentrix Risk Pte Ltd, is based in Singapore and receives card data (tokenised card number, BIN and device data).
Legion policy: any vendor processing payment or card data must store and process it only in India.
Brevis Pay's latest SOC 2 Type II report covers 1 Aug 2024 to 31 Jul 2025, so it is about 14 months old.
Brevis Pay's June 2026 penetration test has one high-severity finding (missing rate limiting on the refund API), open since 20 August 2026 (47 days).
Brevis Pay's India-only hosting add-on moves fraud scoring to its Mumbai region and can be switched on within 3 weeks of ordering.
In October 2025, a misconfigured Brevis log bucket exposed merchant contact data (no card data). Brevis reported it to CERT-In 9 days later.
Legion policy: incidents must be reported to CERT-In within 6 hours, and vendors must notify Legion within 2 hours.
Arvanta reported its November 2025 minor security incident to CERT-In within 5 hours.
Brevis Pay's PCI DSS v4.0 attestation is valid until June 2027; Arvanta's is valid until February 2027.
Brevis enforces MFA and single sign-on on merchant dashboards; Arvanta's MFA is optional for merchant admin users.
Arvanta's annual vendor risk assessment was last done in November 2025 and is due again in November 2026.
Both gateways support RBI card-on-file tokenisation.
Overall payment success rate: Arvanta 97.8% (12 months); Brevis 97.6% (pilot, Aug–Sep 2026).
At Coral Bank and Tamra Bank (18% of volume), Brevis succeeds 94.8% and 95.2% of the time, against Arvanta's 97.5%.
At all other banks (82% of volume), Brevis succeeds 98.2% of the time, against Arvanta's 97.9%.
Uptime over the last 12 months: Arvanta 99.82%, Brevis 99.95%.
95th-percentile payment latency: Arvanta 1.9 seconds, Brevis 1.4 seconds.
Major availability incidents in the last 12 months: Arvanta 3 (including a 4-hour outage on 14 June 2026); Brevis 1.
UPI AutoPay mandate success: Arvanta 96.1% (12 months), Brevis 97.4% (pilot).
Brevis does not support eNACH for two small banks (about 2% of mandates); those must stay on Arvanta.
Internal estimate: migrating to Brevis takes 6 weeks with 4 engineers.
Only 3 payments engineers are free from November 2026, so the 6-week plan is likely to slip to about 8 weeks.
Legion's payment routing layer can split traffic by issuing bank and payment method.
Brevis offers a real-time settlement and reconciliation API; Arvanta provides daily files.
Brevis's sales deck claims migration can be done 'in under 4 weeks'.
